notes: Both occurrences of 'with' placed on the Niphal יִמָּלֵא: 'filled with' is the predicate's own valency (rule 33's מָלֵא clause) and the repetition over the gapped colon 'our tongue with singing' joins the same discontinuous unit (rule 25); the competing reading, each 'with' to its bare noun under rule 33's first sentence, is named in the unit.

הִגְדִּיל לַעֲשׂוֹת divided under rule 56's auxiliary-verb clause (cf. הִרְבָּה לַעֲשׂוֹת → 'wrought much'): 'great things' to the hiphil with the generic 'things' joining under rule 31, 'hath done' to the infinitive the ASV made the English predicate, and the לְ unrepresented (rules 52/40). 'great things' is the ASV's standing rendering of absolute הִגְדִּיל (Joel 2:20–21; 1 Sam 12:24 with no עָשָׂה at all), which supports reading 'things' as the hiphil's generic completion rather than a supplied object of 'done'.
